issue.title: Enhancement: Use wait_until for TSA config check in test_sup_tsa_act_with_sup_reboot to improve test stability.

failure.body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Medium

### Description of the enhancement

Use wait_until for TSA config check in test_sup_tsa_act_with_sup_reboot to improve test stability.

### Current Behavior

After supervisor reboot, the test immediately asserts that the line card's tsa_enabled config in ConfigDB has transitioned to false (TSB). This can fail intermittently if the startup-tsa-tsb service has not yet fully completed and the config has not converged at the time of the check.

### Proposed Behavior

Replace the direct assert with a wait_until poll (120s timeout, 1s interval) to give the startup-tsa-tsb service sufficient time to expire and the ConfigDB tsa_enabled value to transition to false. This makes the test resilient to
timing variations across different platforms and environments. 120 seconds is an umbrella timeout to capture max time allotted for convergence. We have not seen this time-output exceed.

This check runs on every line card in parallel. The wait_until timeout applies per line card, so test duration does not scale with the number of line cards.

### Approach
#### What is the motivation for this PR?
The `test_sup_tsa_act_with_sup_reboot` test intermittently fails because it checks the ConfigDB `tsa_enabled` value immediately after supervisor reboot, without allowing time for the `startup-tsa-tsb` service to complete and the config
to converge.

#### How did you do it?
Replaced the direct `verify_dut_configdb_tsa_value` assert with a `wait_until` poll (120s timeout, 1s interval) that retries until the ConfigDB `tsa_enabled` value transitions to `false`.

#### How did you verify/test it?
Ran the test on a multi-linecard chassis setup and confirmed the `wait_until` poll succeeds after the `startup-tsa-tsb` service completes consistently.
